name: seat-map
title: Seat Map
description: A cinema seat picker split into front, standard and premium price bands. Dragging across a row selects a run of seats, chips show the picks with a running total, and a note warns when a lone seat would be stranded.
use: A ticketing flow needs customers to choose several adjacent seats with clear prices before paying.
avoid: It assumes a cinema layout of rows and blocks, so a different venue shape needs new tier and block props.
a11y: Strong keyboard and screen-reader support; the stranded-seat warning is announced through a live region. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A tall rounded card opens with a film title, showtime line and a 'left' count, then a curved SCREEN arc over rows of small rounded seat squares grouped by price tier. Selected seats turn light, sold ones show diagonal stripes, and picked-seat chips and a wide Continue bar sit below.
behaves: Pressing a free seat and dragging across its row paints every seat between, or removes them if the first was already picked. Picked chips and a total update, and an orange line names any lone seats the booking would strand; beyond the seat limit it refuses more.
customise: Title, subtitle, price tiers, block sizes, sold and wheelchair seats, preselected seats, maximum seats and currency are props, plus change and continue callbacks.
weight: moderate: About a hundred seat buttons plus animated chips and a live stranded-seat recalculation.
demo: The Last Lighthouse, Tonight · 20:15 · Screen 2, with front, standard and premium seats and picks F3 and F4.
issues: Seats are tiny and only show their number once picked, so it is hard to read the grid before choosing.
polishWhy: Thoughtful picker with clear tiers, chips and warnings; the dense grid is very small to read.
